plan.title: Treated vs control DE in human heart (DESeq2 + edgeR)
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is which genes differ between 6 treated and 6 control human heart samples. The data are gene-level counts (Salmon-derived, 12000 genes, first column gene symbol) with no transcript-level quantifications, so the tximport length-offset route is not executable and the model runs directly on the gene-level counts; differential transcript usage is out of scope. Two QC flags shape the plan: sample_01 has a library size ~4x below median, and most libraries show >60% duplication on rRNA-depleted total RNA without UMIs. Neither warrants removal by default: duplication rate follows expression level, so duplicate removal without UMIs deletes true signal; the count models down-weight low depth through size factors. The plan therefore first characterizes sample structure (blind vst, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, per-sample library size and detected-gene counts, duplication-rate context) and only removes sample_01 with a stated reason. DE then runs as the DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage on a minimal 10-count pre-filter, explicit control reference level, and BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and — given the QC concerns and 6 replicates per group — a parallel edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test serves as the second method; the DESeq2-edgeR intersection is reported as the high-confidence set and single-method calls as secondary. A final report carries the reproducibility record, p-value histogram, MA and dispersion diagnostics, and the gene table with both unshrunken and shrunken fold changes ranked on the shrunken value.
